Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation I pulled together a lean mutual action plan (attached) that sequences the MSA, DPA, and order form so we can get you into a dedicated pilot environment by the end of November. Key things to call out up front:

- We need a signed MSA (with a scope-of-work), then DPA sign-off in parallel with SOC2 evidence review.
- Order form signature is gated on procurement POs and billing contact confirmation — our billing team needs the exact legal entity and tax ID before finalizing invoice terms.
- Technical onramp (SSO + network allowlist) can start as soon as we have the order form countersigned; essential to schedule a 2-hour setup window.

Attached: MAP_v2.xlsx (timeline), redlines_v3.pdf (current legal comments), orderform_stub.docx (billing fields to confirm).

Proposed dates (high level):
- MSA circulation / redlines: Oct 20–27
- Legal sign-off & DPA: Oct 28–Nov 5
- Procurement approvals & PO submission: Nov 1–Nov 12
- Order form signature + DocuSign: target Nov 15
- Pilot env provision: Nov 16–20

Can you review the MAP and call out any procurement windows or internal holidays that would shift the PO timeline? If those dates work we’ll route the MSA to Karthik in Legal for a final check and have Vanessa own the procurement cadence.

Thanks —

Thanks for the MAP. Quick legal notes after looking at redlines_v3:pdf —

1) MSA: our standard clause set is OK, but EvoMed has two asks we should resolve before circulation: a) data residency carveout for regulated PHI pipelines (we need clarity if customer will send PHI) and b) a liability cap tweak tied to committed spend for the pilot.

2) DPA: request confirming subprocessors list and whether EvoMed requires a signed SCC appendix (they’re EU-adjacent; confirm whether SCCs or EU Addendum needed).

3) Order form: we must capture the pilot SKUs and an explicit acceptance test (simple script-based perf and correctness checks) — acceptance criteria should be in an appendix referenced by the order form.

If Jordan / Aisha confirm no PHI in the pilot and prefer our standard SCCs, we can compress legal review to one week. If they require a custom clause, add 1–2 weeks.

I’ll prepare a redline that keeps the liability cap keyed to pilot committed spend and add acceptance-test language to the order form stub. Attaching the working redline (redlines_v3.pdf) with inline comments.
